title: GET /api/dashboard/metrics aggregates compliance, resources, risk, vendor, and audit-assurance data into one response
description: dashboard-metrics/index.js joins ClientComplianceSummary (compliance), CloudResource+Finding (resources), the risks collection (risk), client_vendors+vendor_assessments (vendorRisk), and the audit-assurance module's audits/audit_nonconformances collections (audit) — five genuinely separate data sources feeding one payload consumed by AuditOverviewContent.jsx.
preconditions: Seeded org with at least one active framework, one open risk, one vendor with an assessment, one open audit finding
steps: As an authenticated org member, call GET /api/dashboard/metrics
Inspect data.compliance.summary, data.resources.summary, data.risk.summary, data.vendorRisk.summary, data.audit.summary
expectedResult: Each of the five summary blocks reflects the seeded data from its own real collection — e.g. data.risk.summary.openRisks counts treatment.status != 'completed', not a stale or zeroed value.

title: ?projectIds= narrows every board's numbers, including the vendor pipeline joined through client_vendors
description: vendor_assessments has no reliable projectId of its own; fetchVendorAssessmentMetrics scopes via client_vendors.projectId through a $lookup. Verify assessmentsOverdue/pipeline actually changes when projectIds is narrowed, not silently zeroed (the pre-fix behavior for any project-scoped caller).
preconditions: Two projects in the same org, each with a vendor that has an overdue assessment
expectedResult: The first call's data.vendorRisk.assessmentPipeline.overdue counts only projectA's vendor; the second call's count includes both.

title: Risk posture/governance fields are only populated when exactly one project is in scope
description: fetchRiskPostureAndGovernance only calls risk-management-service's risk-center/posture and risk-center/governance (which require a single projectId and 400 without one) when scopedIds resolves to exactly 1 project. With 0 projects selected, or 2+ projects selected, or the RMS unreachable, postureScore/postureTrend/treatmentsOverdue/unownedRisks/acceptancesExpiring must come back null, not 0 or a stale number.
expectedResult: First call returns non-null data.risk.summary.postureScore; second call returns data.risk.summary.postureScore === null and the frontend renders it as '—', never as 0.

title: A cached /api/dashboard/metrics entry is reused for identical params and bypassed for a different filter combination
description: dashboard-cache.js's getCache/setCache key on a hash of {scope, dateFrom, dateTo, severities, frameworkIds}. Identical repeat requests within EXEC_DASH_CACHE_TTL (default 60s) must hit the cache; changing any one filter must produce a cache miss and a fresh aggregation.
steps: Call GET /api/dashboard/metrics twice in immediate succession with identical query params
Insert a new risk in the underlying data, then call again with the same params within 60s
Call again with dateFrom set to a different value
expectedResult: The second call returns the identical (stale) cached payload despite the new risk; the third call (different dateFrom) triggers a fresh aggregation reflecting the new risk.

title: dateFrom/dateTo/severities filter Finding and risks but do not silently no-op CloudResource's compliance-status counts
description: dashboard-metrics/index.js applies dateRangeMatch/severityMatch to the Finding and risks aggregations only, because CloudResource has no createdAt/severity field of its own and its compliance.status reflects current state, not a point-in-time event. Verify resourceBoard's passRate/complianceStatusBreakdown stay constant across date ranges while resource findings-derived numbers change.
steps: Call GET /api/dashboard/metrics with no date filters
Compare data.resources.summary.passRate and data.resources.summary.totalFindings across both calls
expectedResult: passRate/complianceStatusBreakdown are identical across both calls; totalFindings/severityDistribution differ if findings exist outside the 30-day window.

title: GET /api/dashboard/:orgId enforces same-org-or-organization.admin before returning providerCoverage
description: The :orgId route in dashboard-metrics/index.js checks req.permissions.has('organization.admin') OR requestedOrgId === req.orgId before calling fetchProviderCoverage; anything else is a 403.
preconditions: Two distinct orgs, A and B, each with active frameworks
steps: As a user in org A (no organization.admin permission), call GET /api/dashboard/<orgB id>
As the same user, call GET /api/dashboard/<orgA id>
As a user holding organization.admin, call GET /api/dashboard/<orgB id>
expectedResult: First call returns 403 Access denied; second call returns 200 with org A's data; third call returns 200 with org B's data.

title: fetchFrameworkReadiness's ClientFramework query respects the caller's project scope
description: Regression coverage for the fix noted in the source: fetchFrameworkReadiness previously queried ClientFramework org-wide regardless of the selected project(s), feeding the Framework Board's readyCount/avgCoverage/strongest/weakest with unscoped data.
preconditions: Project A has 2 active frameworks; Project B has 1 different active framework
expectedResult: totalActive is 2 and .list contains only Project A's two frameworks — Project B's framework is absent.
